_what: The main title for the PROLOGUE -- the feature's opening title sequence, burned over Nightwish's 'Perfume Of The Timeless' at 0:11. Two cards, not one: `stage: title` is the first beat and `stage: credits` is the second, and the build hard-swaps one for the other so the credit pair arrives after the title has settled. Rendered full-frame and TRANSPARENT by cards/render-cards.mjs from cards/maintitle.html, then composited over the picture by scripts/build_prologue.py.
_copy: REPRODUCED, NOT AUTHORED. The two title lines are the exact string the website's prologue already carries, at ~/src/website/src/data/wolves-intro-sequence.ts (the 78.5 - 94 cue): 'PROJECT BLUEFIN\nseven days to the wolves'. stories/megacut/megacut-cards.json reproduces the same pair for act I's slide, as `title` + `subtitle`. Here `label` takes the first line and `title` the second, because the owner asked for the film's title to be the featured line -- see `_owner`. The lowercase of 'seven days to the wolves' is the authored casing; the card uppercases it in CSS exactly as the site's own line2 rule does, so nothing is rewritten to get there.
_owner: Three instructions, verbatim: (1) 'Seven Days to the Wolves is the title of the whole movie so it should be featured, the project bluefin should be on top, subtle but present'; (2) the credit pair, 'Music by Nightwish' / 'Action by Bungie'; (3) 'Stop at 1:31 and then transition to endless forms'. The first is why the site's two slim treatments are swapped between the lines while the authored ORDER is left alone -- Bluefin stays on top, and takes the small rule instead of the display one. A fourth, on the first cut: "don't forget the blue b", then "the words are fine just color in the b" -- so the eyebrow stays as TYPE rather than becoming the real wordmark, and only the B of BLUEFIN is accented. The blue is #4285f4, the published fill of the fin ligature in Project Bluefin's own mark, so the one coloured letter carries the same value the one coloured element of the real mark does.
_credit_pair: ONE LINE, not two. Owner, 2026-08-16: 'I want to change this: Music by Nightwish | Action by Bungie -- and then put the vertical glow/sear in'. The pipe is the owner's punctuation and is reproduced with the rest of the string; what the card changes is only how that one character is DRAWN -- cards/maintitle.html replaces the typeface's glyph with a vertical rule carrying the film's own blue sear, the same treatment tools/credits.py already burns onto act VIII's call to action. The owner's own words, reproduced as written and NOT uppercased. They are set in the act slide's `.artist` face (cards/act.html) rather than a third typeface. They are a CREDIT, not a rights record: what this film is permitted to do with Nightwish's music video and Bungie's footage lives in videos/yt_nightwish_perfume_of_the_timeless.json and each video record's usage_class, never on a card.
_timing: Windows are FRAME-VERIFIED against media/yt_nightwish_perfume_of_the_timeless.mkv, not assumed from the owner's timestamps. The source's own shot boundaries in this stretch are 12.28-12.56 (the void gives way to the living world), 24.88, 36.32, 40.72, 44.36, 49.64 and 75.64. The title is cued at 11.0 so it is already on screen, over the empty dark, when the world blooms behind it at 12.3 -- the reveal happens THROUGH the title rather than fighting it -- and it clears well before the 24.88 cut.
